'''Karen Marie Brucks''' (February 1, 1957{{r|nams}} – July 8, 2017{{r|sad}}) was an American mathematician known for her research in [[topological dynamics]], and for her advocacy of women in mathematics.{{r|awm}} She worked for many years as a faculty member and administrator at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]].{{r|sad|unt}}

==Life==
Brucks was born on February 1, 1957, in [[Chicago]].{{r|nams}} She majored in mathematics at the [[University of Arizona]], graduating in 1980.{{r|cv}} Next, she earned a master's degree in 1982 at the [[University of North Texas]], and continued there for doctoral study, completing her Ph.D. in 1988.{{r|unt}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Dynamics of One Dimensional Maps'', was supervised by R. Daniel Mauldin.{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral positions at [[Michigan State University]] and [[Stony Brook University]], she became a faculty member at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee in 1991, eventually serving for 24 years there.{{r|sad|unt}} She was a [[Fulbright Scholar]] in 1997–1998, on a research visit to Hungary.{{r|fulbright}} At the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee, she chaired the mathematics department for four years,{{r|sad|unt}} from 2001 to 2005,{{r|cv}} and spent seven years as Associate Dean of Natural Sciences,{{r|sad|unt}} beginning in 2008.{{r|cv|adns}}

She retired as associate professor emeritus in 2015,{{r|sad|unt|retire}} and died on July 8, 2017.{{r|sad}}

==Research==
Brucks's research primarily concerned [[dynamical system]]s, and particularly systems operating on one-dimensional [[Interval (mathematics)|intervals]], including and applications of [[Milnor–Thurston kneading theory]] to [[Unimodality|unimodal]] maps on intervals such as the [[tent map]], [[logistic map]], and  [[Markov odometer|adding machines]]. With Henk Bruin she authored the book ''Topics from one-dimensional dynamics'', published in 2004 by the [[Cambridge University Press]] as volume 62 of their London Mathematical Society Student Texts series.{{r|t1d}}

==Advocacy==
Brucks was a regular instructor in a [[National Science Foundation]] summer program for undergraduate women in mathematics, beginning in 1997.{{r|awm}} She also served on the advisory board for the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee Women in Mathematics, Science, and Engineering Program,{{r|nams}} and was active in leadership in the [[American Association of University Women]],{{r|awm|nams|cv}} [[Association for Women in Mathematics]],{{r|awm|cv}} and [[American Mathematical Society]].{{r|nams}}
